subsystems.name: Memristor crossbar array
subsystems.role: stores each synaptic weight as a cell's resistance and computes sums in place, using Ohm's law for multiplication and Kirchhoff's law for addition.
parts: metal-oxide switching layer (e.g. hafnium or tantalum oxide)

subsystems.name: Selector or access transistor
subsystems.role: isolates each cell so neighbours are not disturbed during reading and writing.

subsystems.name: CMOS periphery
subsystems.role: drives rows, reads tiny currents and converts them back to digital.

subsystems.name: Neuron circuits
subsystems.role: reproduce the soma: accumulate input, fire when a threshold is crossed, then reset.

subsystems.name: Programming and calibration layer
subsystems.role: maps trained weights onto imperfect, drifting conductances.
parts: compiler that maps a neural network onto the array

buildSteps.title: Choose the device stack
buildSteps.detail: Engineers pick the oxide, electrode metals and cell size so that resistance switches reliably at low voltage and holds many distinguishable levels.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the crossbar
buildSteps.detail: Rows and columns of metal lines are patterned at nanometre scale, with the switching oxide deposited between them by atomic layer deposition or sputtering.

buildSteps.title: Integrate on top of CMOS
buildSteps.detail: The array is built in the back-end-of-line above finished CMOS, so drivers and sense amplifiers sit directly beneath the cells without competing for silicon area.

buildSteps.title: Form the filaments
buildSteps.detail: A controlled voltage is applied to each fresh cell to create the conductive filament that makes it switchable — a one-time 'electroforming' step.

buildSteps.title: Tune each weight
buildSteps.detail: Write-verify loops pulse cells and re-read them until each conductance lands close to its target, because cells vary from one another.

buildSteps.title: Train or map the network
buildSteps.detail: Either a network is trained in software and its weights transferred, or the array learns on-chip by strengthening and weakening cells with timed pulses — the hardware version of long-term potentiation.

buildSteps.title: Connect neurons and routing
buildSteps.detail: Neuron circuits and an on-chip network link the crossbar layers into a full network.

buildSteps.title: Test drift and temperature
buildSteps.detail: Engineers measure how conductance wanders over hours and with heat, then build compensation into the compiler.

prerequisites.why: the periphery and access transistors must be small and low-power enough for edge use.
cells work, but pinning a cell to one of dozens of stable levels is still the central difficulty.
two identical cells never behave identically, and conductances creep after programming.
conversion can outweigh the savings from computing in analog if it is inefficient.

prerequisites.tech: Training methods tolerant of hardware noise
prerequisites.why: algorithms must accept approximate weights and still hit target accuracy.

pathway.milestone: embedded resistive memory in commercial microcontrollers, plus research crossbars up to megabit class
pathway.unlocks: non-volatile memory on chip and small in-memory computing demonstrations.

pathway.milestone: hybrid analog-digital accelerator chips that run inference at milliwatt power
on-chip learning demonstrated in a product-like robot
pathway.unlocks: machines that adapt to their environment without cloud training.
brain-scale connectivity with far less energy spent moving data.
